section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces research investigating whether insight problem solving predicts real-world creativity, contrasting it with divergent thinking. Two studies were conducted: Study 1 (n=133) focused on creative achievement, and Study 2 (n=173) examined everyday creative behavior. Both studies also assessed personality and fluid intelligence. The findings indicated no relationship between insight problem solving and creativity, but significant effects were observed for openness to experience and fluid intelligence.

SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: In two studies, we explored the contribution of several classic insight problems in creative achievement (Study 1; n - 133) and everyday creative behavior (Study 2; n - 173).

ES.evidence_source: Both studies found no evidence for a relationship between insight problem solving and creative behavior and achievement.

Effects.evidence_source: No correlation coefficients (Pearson r) between intelligence scores and creative achievement (CAQ or ICAA) were found in the text or table.

Measure IQ.evidence_source: We also assessed the role of personality and fluid intelligence, two well-established predictors of real-world creativity, to determine their relative influence beyond the effect of insight. For example, fluid intelligence (Gf)—a general cognitive ability associated with domain-general reasoning and controlled attention (Kane et al., 2004)—predicts the creative quality of ideas generated during divergent thinking (Nusbaum & Silvia, 2011) and novel metaphor production (Beaty & Silvia, 2013; Silvia & Beaty, 2012).

section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces two studies investigating the relationship between insight problem solving and real-world creativity. Study 1, with 133 participants, focused on creative achievement, while Study 2, with 173 participants, examined everyday creative behavior. Both studies also considered personality and fluid intelligence as predictors. The findings indicated no relationship between insight problem solving and creativity, but fluid intelligence and openness to experience were significant predictors. Table 1, titled 'Insight Problems and Between-Person Solution Rates: Study 1 and Study 2', presents the percentage of participants who solved various insight problems for both studies, along with the number of participants in parentheses.
